items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: And we had several good players, but it was limited. ... there was another fella by the name of Henry Beckett who played beautiful trombone.

ctx.x: musicians at any chance that they got. And so by meeting Lester Young and Joe Jones, I was inspired, and as I was inspired naturally you wanted to go onto better things. And none of these orchestras that I played with had a full amount of men who were qualified to be good players.

We had perhaps like one or two good solo men like Buddy Tate, and maybe a trumpet player or trombone player. Like Henry Coker played trombone. And there was another fella by the name of Henry Beckett who played beautiful trombone. He had a sound like Tommy Dorsey and he played with a feeling of the blues, you know. And we had several good players, but it was limited.
